summary: Wilcox County 100-foot steel tower the Register dates to Oct-Nov 1941, built by a CCC camp it calls Vrendeburgh (unconfirmed elsewhere); registered 2021; condition unsourced.

events.note: Register says workers from the Vrendeburgh CCC camp built it in October and November 1941; no other source found names that camp

evidence.supports: 100-foot steel tower built by workers from a CCC camp in October and November 1941
evidence.quote: This 100-foot steel tower was built by workers from the Vrendeburgh CCC camp in October and November 1941.

evidence.supports: Vredenburgh is a town in Monroe County; the part read names no CCC camp
evidence.quote: Vredenburgh is located Monroe County in the southwest region of the state.

evidence.supports: CCC stopped building fire towers at US entry into WWII, leaving some unfinished
evidence.quote: the Civilian Conservation Corps ceased building firetowers, leaving a number standing unfinished as Corps workers went to fight.

evidence.supports: Forestry personnel took over the tower building afterward
evidence.quote: Forestry personnel took over, building new towers both during the war and a few decades beyond.

evidence.supports: by 1942 the CCC had built 61 lookout towers in Alabama
evidence.quote: By 1942, the CCC had built 1,800 miles of roads, 61 lookout towers, 490 bridges

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: One register source (read in full) for the 1941 build, the CCC camp and the 2021 registration. The camp name 'Vrendeburgh' matched no source found. Searches surfaced Vredenburgh, a Monroe County mill town (EOA), and the part of that entry read names no CCC camp; the spelling may be a typo for Vredenburgh, or the camp may be unrelated. Unconfirmed, and the story does not state the link as fact. The register gives no managing agency. Standing status, staffing, access and condition are unsourced. The 100-foot height (30.5 m) is the Register's tower height and may not be cab-floor height. A search for a 1941 Alabama tower returned Rock Mountain (Jefferson County), a different tower, excluded.
